question: What is the main focus of holistic nursing care?

options.A: Administering prescribed medications on a strict schedule
options.B: Managing hospital equipment and monitoring vital signs
options.C: Treating the whole person including mind, body, and spirit
options.D: Focusing strictly on curing the diagnosed physical disease

explanation: Holistic nursing looks beyond just the physical symptoms to care for every aspect of the human person. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T2#GNS123_U1_T2_h1)

question: How does holistic care differ from traditional medical care that only looks at the disease?

options.A: It focuses only on spiritual counseling during illness
options.B: It integrates physical treatments with emotional and social support
options.C: It completely replaces modern medicine with herbal remedies
options.D: It ignores laboratory results in favor of patient feelings

explanation: Great job! Holistic care doesn't throw out medicine; it simply combines standard medical treatments with a broad view of everything our patients need.

question: Which dimension of holistic care involves a person's sense of meaning, purpose, and faith?
explanation: The spiritual dimension connects a patient to their core values, life purpose, and faith traditions. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T2#GNS123_U1_T2_h2)

question: A patient with severe malaria is worried about losing income and how their family will eat while they are in the hospital. Which dimension of care is primarily affected here?
explanation: Spot on! Family roles, financial worries, and community support fall squarely under the social dimension of human life.

question: Which of these is a great example of an open-ended question you can ask a patient?

options.A: Asking 'How are you coping with your illness today?'
options.B: Nodding silently without asking any questions at all
options.C: Asking 'Did you take your morning blood pressure pill?'
options.D: Telling the patient 'You need to stop worrying so much.'

explanation: Well done! Open-ended questions can't be answered with a simple 'yes' or 'no', which encourages your patient to open up and share more.

question: Why is building a trusting nurse-patient relationship so important for holistic care?

options.A: It allows the nurse to give orders that the patient must follow without question
options.B: It ensures the patient will never complain about hospital food or bills
options.C: It helps patients feel safe enough to share deep fears and personal concerns
options.D: It replaces the need for doctors to visit the patient on the ward

explanation: You got it! Trust creates a safe space where patients feel comfortable revealing the emotional and social burdens that impact their healing.

question: Which of these is a key part of doing a full, holistic nursing assessment?

options.A: Exploring the patient's home support systems and cultural beliefs
options.B: Avoiding questions about mental health to prevent upsetting them
options.C: Rushing the patient to finish answering interview questions quickly
options.D: Focusing exclusively on laboratory values and bedside monitors

explanation: Awesome! Holistic assessments intentionally gather data on social, cultural, and emotional factors right alongside physical signs.

question: Why must a nurse pay attention to non-verbal cues like facial expressions during an assessment?

options.A: Patients may hide their true emotional distress behind polite words
options.B: Non-verbal cues are the only way to measure blood pressure accurately
options.C: Patients expect nurses to read their minds without asking questions
options.D: Hospital regulations require charting body language every hour

explanation: Exactly! People often say they are fine while their body language quietly reveals anxiety, pain, or fear.

question: What is an important safety action when a patient wants to use herbal supplements in the hospital?

options.A: Encourage the patient to double their dosage for faster healing
options.B: Confiscate all herbal products immediately because they are dangerous
options.C: Ignore what the patient takes as long as they swallow their pills
options.D: Screen the supplements for potential interactions with prescribed medications

explanation: Spot on! Herbal products can react strongly with conventional drugs, so as nurses, we always check for safety interactions first.

question: What is the primary role of the nurse when patients want to use complementary or alternative therapies?

options.A: Forbidding patients from using any therapy not written in the doctor's orders
options.B: Personally performing massage and aromatherapy for every single patient
options.C: Ensuring safe use, providing education, and supporting patient preferences
options.D: Selling herbal supplements to patients to help fund the hospital ward

explanation: Well done! Nurses act as educators and safety advocates, helping patients safely blend alternative methods with their standard medical care.

question: What makes a nursing care plan truly 'individualized' in holistic practice?

options.A: Writing the care plan in medical jargon the patient cannot understand
options.B: Leaving all care planning decisions entirely up to the attending physician
options.C: Using the exact same printed template for every patient with malaria
options.D: Tailoring goals and interventions to the patient's unique lifestyle and values

explanation: That's right! An individualized care plan respects the specific background, preferences, and personal goals of each unique patient.

question: An elderly patient refuses to eat the standard hospital diet because it feels strange to them. What is the best holistic nursing action?

options.A: Report the patient to the medical director for being uncooperative
options.B: Collaborate with the patient to include familiar, culturally accepted local foods
options.C: Force-feed the patient to ensure they meet their daily caloric requirements
options.D: Discharge the patient immediately for refusing hospital dietary guidelines

explanation: Spot on! Holistic care respects cultural preferences and partners with the patient to find workable, comforting dietary solutions.

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to holistic nursing practice in busy hospitals?

options.A: Hierarchical medical structures that limit nursing autonomy
options.B: Abundant staffing levels with too many nurses on every shift
options.C: Task-oriented routines focused only on quick medication rounds
options.D: Heavy workloads and high patient-to-nurse ratios

explanation: Great catch! Staff shortages and heavy workloads are major barriers in our hospitals, so abundant staffing is definitely not one of them.

question: How can you deliver holistic care even when working in a busy, understaffed ward?

options.A: By refusing to admit any new patients until the workload lightens
options.B: By delegating all patient contact completely to hospital security guards
options.C: By ignoring all physical medication duties to focus entirely on meditation
options.D: By weaving compassionate communication and a reassuring touch into routine tasks

explanation: Brilliant! Holism doesn't always require extra time. You can easily integrate it into regular nursing duties like bathing a patient or administering medications.
